posts.title: Halloween special XIV: The fossils that haunted Lovecraft
posts.description: In November 1923, newspapers such as The New York Times reported on a desert whose name was unfamiliar to most Westerners: the Gobi. posts.title: Forgotten Women of Palaeontology: Ekaterina Lermontova
posts.description: Ekaterina (or Yekaterina) Vladimirovna Lermontova was born on February 11, 1889, in Saint Petersburg, Russia, into a distinguished intellectual family. Her lineage included the romantic poet Mikhail Yurievich Lermontov (1814–1841) and the chemist Julia Vsevolodovna Lermontova (1846–1919), the first Russian woman to earn a doctorate in chemistry. posts.title: Antusuchus rionegrinus: a predator in the Kokorkom Desert
posts.description: Almost 100 million years ago, the Kokorkom Desert stretched across the region now occupied by the provinces of Río Negro and Neuquén in Argentina; it was a vast system of mobile dunes in a hot and arid climate, shaped by the wind.
